# Hardware-Assisted Projection

Also called: Hardware-Accelerated Cell Projection, GPU-Based Projected Tetrahedra

## Overview
Hardware-Assisted Projection is a family of volume rendering techniques that accelerate the cell projection method by offloading scan conversion and compositing to the graphics pipeline [S1, book]. It solves the performance bottleneck of software-based ray integration by projecting 3D cells into screen space and using hardware rasterization for interpolation [S1, book]. Unlike pure raycasting, it requires explicit back-to-front sorting of cells to ensure correct alpha blending, distinguishing it from sorting-free additive methods [S1, book].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family share the core mechanism of projecting volumetric cells (tetrahedra, polyhedra, or hexahedra) onto the 2D image plane and utilizing the GPU's polygon rasterization pipeline [S1, book].

1.  **Projection**: 3D cell vertices are transformed into screen space. The cell's projection is decomposed into rasterizable primitives (triangles or polygons) [S1, book].
2.  **Attribute Computation**: For each primitive vertex, the geometric thickness $l$ (length of the viewing ray segment within the cell) and scalar values (extinction coefficient $\tau$ or density) at the entry and exit points are computed [S1, book].
3.  **Hardware Interpolation**: The rasterizer interpolates these attributes across the screen-space primitive [S1, book].
4.  **Opacity/Color Evaluation**: The interpolated values are used to compute opacity and color. To avoid artifacts from linear interpolation of non-linear opacity, methods use either:
    *   Texture mapping for exponential lookup of transparency $T = \exp(-\int \tau ds)$ [S1, book].
    *   Pre-integration textures storing the result of the volume ray integral for arbitrary transfer functions [S1, book].
5.  **Compositing**: The resulting fragments are composited using the Porter-Duff "over" operator in back-to-front order [S1, book].

## Subtopics

### [Hardware-Assisted Polyhedron Projection](1453-hardware-assisted-polyhedron-projection.md)
Handles arbitrary convex polyhedral cells. Requires explicit global back-to-front sorting and winged-edge subdivision of projections to handle non-convex silhouettes.

### [Hardware-Assisted Projected Tetrahedra](1729-hardware-assisted-projected-tetrahedra.md)
Specialized for tetrahedral meshes. Uses a single-pass GPU pipeline with geometry shaders to decompose point primitives into triangles and evaluate the ray integral per fragment.

### [Röttger 3D Texture Mapping](7896-r-ttger-3d-texture-mapping.md)
Extends projected tetrahedra using 3D pre-integration textures to support arbitrary non-linear transfer functions, approximated via 2D texture hardware.

### [Absorption-Only Radiography via Unsorted Hexahedron Projection](10255-absorption-only-radiography-via-unsorted-hexahedron-projecti.md)
Relaxes the sorting requirement for absorption-only rendering by accumulating optical thickness additively in a floating-point buffer, supporting curvilinear hexahedra directly.

### Pre-sorted Tetrahedral Rendering
A variant where cells are sorted before splitting into tetrahedra, using 2D texture mapping to accelerate opacity interpolation [S1, book]. It avoids artifacts from linear interpolation but is limited to linear transfer functions [S1, book].

## Background
The method originates from the need to accelerate unstructured volume visualization. Stein et al. [312] introduced sorting cells before splitting into tetrahedra and using 2D texture mapping for opacity [S1, book]. Röttger et al. [272] later introduced pre-integrated volume rendering to support arbitrary transfer functions using 3D texture maps [S1, book]. The approach builds on the foundational Projected Tetrahedra algorithm [877-projected-tetrahedra.md].
